shots.purpose: One lap that costs him. Establish his pace, let the pace be the thing that wrecks him, and land the wreck right beside Zenny so the audience sees exactly who is the bigger bee and who is the competent one. The joke is not the crash — it is the face he pulls when he realises he got away with it.
shots.performanceAssignment: He leaves at pace, chest driving ahead of his own wings, antennae proud-erect, mouth working the work song at full throttle, and goes crazy off into the distance on a wide erratic arc — shrinking to a fast dot skimming the far flower tops, never leaving frame. He comes back HARDER than he left and completely misjudges it. THE FIRST CRASH IS A REAL SMASH, NOT A BRUSH: he goes FACE-FIRST into a big flower head at full speed and the bloom ENGULFS him — he disappears into the petals entirely for a beat, the whole flower head rocking on its stem — then he bursts back out the other side completely coated in thick gold, trailing it behind him. Still travelling and half-blind with pollen he clips a second bloom, which turns him over, and the turn becomes THREE fast tight somersaults, limbs tucked, the chaos suddenly reading as accidental acrobatics — all of it at flower height, in among the blooms, never up in open sky. He comes out of the third rotation and STICKS THE LANDING on a sturdy flower head like a gymnast finishing a routine: feet planting hard, ONE LEG TUCKED BACK for balance, utterly still for a beat. Then he stands up out of it, brushes the pollen off his chest with one quick embarrassed glance round to check whether anyone saw — and, finding he is completely fine, throws a full SUPERHERO POSE: chest out, fists planted, chin up, shoulders squared, entirely too pleased with himself for a bee who just crashed twice. The line lands on that pose. Zenny's own line through this is simple and continuous: she watches him go, gives up on him, settles to her clover and works head-down through the entire wreck without once looking up at it. She is never still — she is BUSY.
shots.camera: ONE HELD POSITION FOR ALMOST THE WHOLE TAKE, THEN ONE MOTIVATED MOVE. The camera opens front-on on the pair and STAYS THERE — holding the flowers and Zenny in frame while Fuzzby goes crazy off and comes back. He CLEARS THE FRAME entirely on his way out, on a readable vector; the camera does not follow and does not go looking. The frame is not dead while he is gone — ZENNY TRACKS HIM OUT WITH HER EYES, then gives up on him and settles onto the clover beneath her to work. He returns from THE SAME SIDE he left on, at the same height, faster than he went — never from nowhere, never from the opposite edge. It does not chase him, does not go looking, and never climbs off the meadow into open sky: everything, including the tumble, plays at flower height with the blooms and Zenny in shot. It may breathe and reframe a few inches to keep the wreck and Zenny both in frame, nothing more. THE ONE REAL MOVE comes last: after his line lands, the camera DOLLIES IN on Zenny, leaving him behind in the frame, and finishes on her.
shots.openingPose: Both bees hovering at flower-top height in the open field, seen from the FRONT at the same distance from the lens — Fuzzby left of centre and clearly the larger, Zenny to his right and smaller, the size gap plainly readable because they share a depth. Low sun flaring in behind them, open sky above the flower tops, lavender spikes, white daisies and clover heads crowding the frame below them. Wings working hard on both. He is already loading to go; she is still hovering, about to settle onto the clover beneath her. Then he goes — straight off at full pace, out and away across the field, leaving her exactly where she is.
shots.cutInMotivation: This is the one junction the treatment protects on meaning alone: the dip, the sideways drag and the leaf's spring are ONE cause, and a cut anywhere inside them turns a single continuous physics chain into two unrelated events — the audience would read bad luck instead of overcommitment, and the whole reversal loses its author.
shots.dialogueBinding: Fuzzby's vocal beat performs per the approved voice design.
shots.visualPayoff: Fuzzby in a full superhero pose on the flower head — chest out, fists planted, chin up — dusty and delighted; then the camera leaves him and settles on Zenny alone. Her eyes find him first. Her chest rises and falls in one long, entirely deadpan sigh. Her face does not change. She holds that flatness a beat too long — and only then, as she turns fractionally back toward the lens, does ONE CORNER of her mouth go, dry and private, the smallest wry admission that he is hers. The shot lands on that corner moving, not on a finished smile.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Fuzzby's whole body, his wings and his spectacles stay OUTSIDE the blossom and readable in silhouette through every contact — only his face and the front of his chest ever touch the pollen centre. He is never swallowed by a flower, never hidden inside it, never morphed into it.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: THE CRASH IS THE BIGGEST PHYSICAL EVENT IN THE SHOT AND IT IS BUILT IN STAGES, EACH ONE CAUSING THE NEXT: he comes in far too fast and too low; a stem clips his trailing wing and his whole body YAWS off its line; one wing corrects far too late; his face slaps square into the pollen centre of a big bloom at full speed. THE FLOWER TAKES THE FORCE, AND THAT IS WHERE THE SIZE OF THE CRASH LIVES: the head compresses flat under him, the stem bows most of the way to the ground, petals splay back, and a fat cloud of gold erupts out sideways — then the stem whips upright again and flings him off it. Neighbouring blooms are knocked nodding by the blast. He stays outside the bloom and visible for all of it. Still travelling and half-blind with gold, he clips a second head, which turns him over — the three somersaults are momentum, not choice. The landing is a hard plant onto a sturdy flower head, one leg tucked back — the head dips deep under him and rebounds, and he rides that rebound with small balance corrections. Nothing about him goes still; a stuck landing is tension held, not motion stopped. Every contact happens at flower height, in among the blooms.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A dusty bee in a full superhero pose on a flower, delighted with himself — and then the smaller bee alone in frame, who looks, sighs, stays flat, and lets one corner of her mouth go at the very last moment.
prohibitedStaging: never take the tumble up into open sky — it plays at flower height, in the blooms
never let Zenny leave frame at any point
never let the flower swallow or hide him — his body and wings stay outside it
never let her final smile become broad, warm or delighted — it escapes one corner only
no glow, no sparkle trail, no magic light on either bee
never write the landing as still, frozen or dead-still — it is a held pose with the flower rebounding, wings beating and balance correcting inside it

shots.tempoDesign: SEVEN BEATS AND THE SECONDS EACH ONE OWNS. 0.0-1.0s: the pair together, wings working, frame locked on them. 1.0-3.0s: he goes crazy off at pace and CLEARS THE FRAME; Zenny's eyes track him out, then she gives up on him and settles to her clover. He returns from the same side, at the same height. 3.0-5.5s — THE CRASH, THE BIGGEST EVENT IN THE SHOT: stem clips his wing, body yaws, wing corrects too late, face slaps the pollen centre; the head compresses flat, the stem bows to the ground, petals splay, gold erupts sideways, then the stem whips up and flings him off. 5.5-7.0s: second bloom turns him over; THREE somersaults, readable as three, at flower height. 7.0-8.5s: he STICKS the landing, one leg tucked back — a gymnast's stuck finish, tension HELD and never motion stopped: the flower dips and rebounds under him and his balance rides it. 8.5-10.5s: stands, brushes himself down with one quick embarrassed glance round to see if anyone saw, then snaps into the SUPERHERO POSE — the final spoken section lands on it. 10.5-12.0s — HER BUTTON, AND IT IS A LADDER, NOT AN EXPRESSION: the camera dollies off him onto Zenny alone. Eyes first — she finally looks up at him. Then the breath — one long deadpan sigh, chest rising and falling. Then nothing: the face stays flat, a beat longer than is comfortable. ONLY THEN does one corner of her mouth go, dry and wry, and the shot LANDS ON THAT CORNER MOVING — never on a completed smile. Perception, then breath, then the escape. Never all at once, and never broad.
shots.feltIntent: A four-year-old's stomach learns Fuzzby's pace, then feels it go wrong — a faceful of flower they did not see coming, then three somersaults, then a landing he has absolutely no right to. They laugh at the crash; they laugh harder at the superhero pose, because he is posing about an accident. The parent's laugh is the last frame: the small one looking down the lens like the only adult in the room.
shots.continuityProseOut: Zenny alone in frame at her blossom, head up, mid-turn back toward the lens, face otherwise flat with one corner of her mouth just going; Fuzzby soft behind her, still in his superhero pose on the flower head, pollen still drifting.
shots.dialogueTimingProse: Fuzzby's work song runs across the flight out and the turn back, and dies into the first crash — roughly 3-4 seconds of song, ending the moment his face hits the pollen; no dialogue across the tumble or the landing, which play in the impacts and the buzz. The final line lands ON the superhero pose. Zenny's sigh and the escape of her smile come after it, in the buzz, with her mouth closed throughout.
shots.referenceRolesProse: Fuzzby anchor (identity: spectacles, bulbous tan nose, translucent wings, antennae) and Zenny anchor for the second bee (identity plus the size gap — Fuzzby clearly the bigger); size chart for the two-bee relationship; Buzzing Nook / wildflower scene anchor plus the scene's approved Scene Look for the field's palette, materials and light.
shots.principalPerformanceApproved: Fuzzby sings the work song at full throttle while his body performs professionalism nobody asked for — chest driving forward, antennae proud-erect, wings fast and continuous, altitude overshooting the climb then undershooting the fall. He does not aim at the blossom so much as attack it, and he commits harder than the job needs because in his head this is a display.
shots.animationTimingApproved: Fast and accelerating from the first frame: the zig-zag climb runs on quick, uneven up-down beats with no two the same length, tightening as he closes on the blossom. The dip is the one deliberate loading action — a hair longer than the beats around it. From the anthers' dump to the leaf's bow the chain runs continuous with no gaps at the joins: the sideways drag is a fast slide, the leaf's bow is heavy and slow-in as it takes his weight, and its rebound is a hard snap out. The impact runs in a stretched slow pocket of roughly a beat — everything moving, nothing held — then returns to full speed for the recovery, which builds over about a second and a half, the chest first, the head last. The drooped antenna's follow-through settles a beat AFTER the stance has finished, so the tell arrives on its own timing. Wings beat fast and continuous through every phase, including the slow pocket.

voiceDirectorBrief.physicalActionRelationship: Voice and body telling the same lie together: the syllables land on the up-beats of the porpoise so the song sounds like it is steering him, when the flight is steering the song. The final trailing syllable coincides with the flank meeting the leaf, so the tune gets bent by the bow rather than finished.

voiceDirectorBrief.speaker: Fuzzby
voiceDirectorBrief.expectedTiming: Lands early in the shot, on the held pose, with the gold still falling past him; the eye-flick and the antenna's failed rise play out in the silence after.
voiceDirectorBrief.physicalActionRelationship: Delivered while the pose keeps building — chest pushing out one notch further on the line, glasses shedding gold, small mid-air corrections under him, wings fast beneath the dignity. The eye-flick to the drooped antenna comes AFTER the line, so the confession never contaminates the claim.

SOURCE MATERIAL — storyboard-approved facts for the cinematic card. This is NOT a prompt and must never fire; the register card is written from it at the Animation gate.
SET & LIGHT LAW (light is written in THIS vocabulary — concrete sky/sun/shadow states, never time-of-day words): Stylised feature-quality 3D CGI matching @图1. Original 3D CGI animation, ages 4-8, Pixar-caliber: real weight, squash-and-stretch, bold legible staging, character locked to reference.
REFERENCES: Use @图2 only for Zenny, @图3 only for Fuzzby and @图4 only for the round set.
FELT INTENT (the one feeling every camera, light and performance choice serves): A four-year-old's stomach learns Fuzzby's rhythm before it learns his face: stems whipping past close enough to swipe, light strobing, a body that keeps overrunning its own tempo. When the leaf throws him back out they laugh at the surprise; the parent has been reading the crowded top of frame as a promise since the first second.
OPENING ANCHOR: Begin exactly on @图1, the approved opening frame — motion begins immediately, never a resting hold.
CAMERA (storyboard-approved): The camera is his overexcited wingman: behind him, banking with him, deliberately half a beat late, horizon rolling as he rolls, and near-field leaves passing close enough to swipe the lens. It genuinely loses him at the dip behind a near-field leaf and rediscovers him already sideways and in trouble — the loss is the point, so his speed reads as something the frame cannot contain. Through the FWIP the camera must be thrown by the leaf's spring rather than choose the move: every inch of travel here has a visible physical cause in frame. Zenny must be findable, small and unremarked, in the deep background of the recovery without the camera going to look for her.
OPENING POSE / FIRST FRAME: Bee-height inside a corridor of tall rainforest flowers, the camera already travelling forward and slightly behind Fuzzby — his pollen-loaded body pitched away from us into a rising zig-zag, wings a fast blur, a rope of gold dust trailing off his hind legs, and in the near foreground a stem swinging back across the lens where he has just clipped it. Canopy shafts strobe over him as he climbs toward a ceiling of leaves that leaves him almost no headroom.
PERFORMANCE (approved physical performance): He flies the corridor as a display rather than a commute — chest driving ahead of his own wings, antennae carried proud-erect like rank, mouth working the work song at full throttle, and every zig-zag climbing higher than the flowers need before dropping lower than they need, so he is porpoising up and down inside his own zig-zag with the leaf ceiling threatening his back the whole way. He aims his head, not his line, at the blossom and drives it in past its centre; the anthers dump their loose gold onto his braced hind legs, and the new weight hanging off his back end swings his exit line sideways so he leaves the bloom flank-first and travelling wrong. His flank meets the broad leaf, the leaf's stalk takes him and bows low, and the bow's rebound throws him back up the corridor with the loose gold shearing off him. He arrests himself inside his own falling cloud and rebuilds the on-parade stance from the chest outward — shoulders back, head lifting last, wings still beating fast beneath a body that has decided to be dignified — while one antenna stays folded over and does not come up with its partner. The impact stretches into one slow pocket at the leaf — antenna whipping slow, gold hanging in the air, wings still beating fast through it — then snaps back to full speed for the recovery stance. Nothing freezes; the tempo runs slow and comes back.
INTERNAL CUTS (each becomes its own 'Shot N:' segment of the card, in this order):
  1. push closer as the zig-zag climbs into its overshoot
  2. reframe wider on the leaf's bend and spring so the throw has room to travel

The dip is the one deliberate loading action — a hair longer than the beats around it. From the anthers' dump to the leaf's bow the chain runs continuous with no gaps at the joins: the sideways drag is a fast slide, the leaf's bow is heavy and slow-in as it takes his weight, and its rebound is a hard snap out. The impact runs in a stretched slow pocket of roughly a beat — everything moving, nothing held — then returns to full speed for the recovery, which builds over about a second and a half, the chest first, the head last. The drooped antenna's follow-through settles a beat AFTER the stance has finished, so the tell arrives on its own timing. Wings beat fast and continuous through every phase, including the slow pocket.
GAG PHYSICS — stays visible: His wings, spectacles and the silhouette of his back through the dip
GAG PHYSICS — contact and weight: His body enters the blossom past its centre; the anthers dump loose gold onto his hind legs and the added weight pulls his exit line sideways; his flank, not his head, meets the broad leaf; the leaf's stalk compresses and bends low under his full weight, then rebounds and throws him back out along the corridor while the loose gold shears off him in a cloud. The leaf keeps oscillating after he has gone.
GAG PHYSICS — payoff shape: A proud on-parade bee hanging mid-air inside a cloud of his own spilled cargo, one antenna drooped, the leaf that threw him still shaking behind his head.
GAG PHYSICS — prohibited staging: ['never let the leaf appear to strike him — his own sideways momentum must deliver him into it', "never cut between the dip, the sideways drag and the leaf's spring", 'never let the gold cloud hide his silhouette or his glasses', 'never let his hover go level and controlled at any point in the climb']

CONTINUITY OUT: world (lighting + camera side): Loose gold hangs in the air where he was thrown, the broad leaf is still oscillating on its stalk, one of his antennae is folded over and has not come back up, and far down the corridor Zenny is already at her own blossom with full sacks, head down. | Fuzzby (screenZone/facing/pose/expression): Hovering in a chest-out on-parade stance inside his own falling gold cloud, one antenna erect and one folded over, wings still beating fast. | Zenny (screenZone/facing/pose/expression): Small and soft in the deep background, settled at her blossom with full pollen sacks, head down, not looking up.

shots.purpose: Button the ricochet with the cover-up, in a frame where the world is still visibly contradicting the claim — and let the boast land at nobody, so the beat hands over a need for a witness.
shots.performanceAssignment: He is holding a pose he has decided is a posture: chest pumped forward and shoulders pinned back, the whole upper body carried in place by effort rather than at rest, with tiny hover corrections drifting him a fraction up and down and his wings beating fast and continuous beneath the dignity. Everything he does is the work of maintaining the claim — jaw set, head high, eyes fixed out front as he delivers the reclaim without any part of the pose loosening. Once, his eyes drop to the folded antenna and come straight back out front, and the head lifts a degree higher to compensate; he flexes the antenna upward from its base, it rises halfway, then folds over again and he refuses to look at it a second time. As the last of the gold sifts past his shoulder his eyes travel off down the corridor to where the other bee is working, and the chest stays pumped while they go.
shots.camera: The camera stops travelling and stays with him at close range because it has just been thrown here — it is out of breath, not composed. What must stay true is that the world keeps contradicting him inside his own frame: the falling gold and the leaf's dying oscillation stay in shot with him for the whole reclaim, so the boast is never allowed a clean background to be true in.
shots.openingPose: Tight on Fuzzby from slightly below, chest-out and mid-air against bright background haze, gold dust still drifting down through frame past him and the tip of the oscillating leaf clipping into the lower edge behind his shoulder.
shots.cutInMotivation: Staying continuous from the FWIP would keep the audience inside his motion, and the joke needs the motion to STOP so the deadpan claim can sit in the air; the cut also changes what we know — we are now watching him rather than riding him, which is the first time the frame has an opinion about him.
shots.visualPayoff: Fuzzby hanging in his proud stance with the gold nearly settled out of frame, one antenna sagging while the other stays erect, his eyes going off down the corridor toward the far blossom where the other bee is working.

shots.tempoDesign: Instant on the pose — no wind-up, he is already proud when the cut lands, which is the joke. Then the shot spends its time doing almost nothing at speed: hover corrections small and quick, wings continuous, while the gold takes the full length of the shot to fall past him. The eye-flick to the antenna is fast in, fast out, and the compensating head-lift arrives a beat after it, too late to help. The antenna's attempted rise is slow up and quick down — the collapse is the sharper of the two. The final eye-travel down the corridor is slow and is the last movement in the shot, arriving after the gold has cleared.
shots.feltIntent: The kid hears the flattest little brag in the meadow and giggles at the nerve of it. The parent notices there is nobody in front of him to hear it, and that the drooped antenna already knows.

shots.purpose: Escalate the moment he has a witness — the face-plunge into the flower and the moustache it lays on him, delivered as one unbroken piece of physics so the gold is a consequence and not a trick.
shots.performanceAssignment: He arrives already committed and buries his face in the anthers, and then keeps shoving — shoulders working the head deeper as though thoroughness were measured in depth, hind legs planting and re-planting on the petal rim for purchase while both wings beat fast outside the petals and his rear end wags with the effort. The rim gives, his own shove runs out, and he hauls back the way he came, the reverse dragging his whole face across the loaded anthers as it goes. Clear of the bloom he does not check himself; he swings the chest forward, drags the shoulders back and lifts the head last into the largest on-parade stance he has struck yet, both antennae snapping proud-erect, and puts the question out front with total conviction — eyes wide open, looking at nothing on his own face, hover holding by small quick corrections while loose gold sifts off his shoulders. Nothing in him examines the result.
shots.camera: The camera stays close alongside the bloom and follows the plunge in and the reverse out on his own body's movement, then falls back a touch as he rises so the band of gold across his face is unmistakable at the moment he speaks. It must never cut away between the plunge and the reveal — the in and the out are one physical sentence — and it must never look ahead to the other bee, because his blindness to her verdict is the setup.
shots.openingPose: Bee-height alongside a wide open bloom, the camera arriving with Fuzzby as he comes in fast from behind the lens — his forward-driving silhouette crossing into frame and burying its face in the packed anthers, rear half and two beating wings left outside the petals, the bloom rocking on its stem from the hit.
shots.cutInMotivation: Remaining continuous from his boast would let the escalation read as more of the same ride; a fresh setup at the new bloom buys acceleration and a new visual idea — this is the beat where the pollen stops being cargo, and it deserves its own arrival rather than being inherited.
shots.dialogueBinding: Fuzzby's vocal beat performs per the approved voice design.
shots.visualPayoff: Fuzzby in a full chest-out on-parade stance just clear of the bloom, a thick band of gold laid across his face under his spectacles, antennae proud-erect, the flower he came out of still rocking behind him and loose pollen sifting off his shoulders.

shots.purpose: Abandon him mid-boast for her — the ride hits the wall. Her withholding, her ruling and the covered antenna-dip, in the flatter grammar that shuts the door on his momentum.
shots.performanceAssignment: She is working, and she keeps working: her forepaws are packing gold down into her own sacks in small even strokes, one sack shifting a fraction as it fills, while her flat stare stays aimed off-frame at him and does not move with the packing. The withholding is a task she performs — she lets his question go unanswered while she finishes a stroke, then another, sitting on the silence a fraction past comfortable, breathing shallow, eyelids low, one shoulder settling as her weight redistributes over the leaf. When she does answer, only her mouth moves and the stare does not adjust; her paws pause exactly on the last word, and one slow blink arrives after it, closing and opening late. On the final beat her antennae dip a fraction toward him, she catches it, brings them level, and drops her eyes back down to the sacks, the paws resuming the same small even strokes.
shots.camera: This frame does not move and that is the entire editorial opinion — no drift, no reassurance push-in, no consolation reframe, because the moment it breathes the two grammars stop colliding and this becomes ordinary chase coverage. Stillness is FOR the door shutting on his momentum; what stays alive inside it is her: the aim of her stare, the delay she is choosing to impose, her paws still working the sacks, and the tiny dip she catches herself making. He must stay off-screen for her ruling — his boast bought this frame and gets none of it.

shots.cutInMotivation: This cut buys the scene's core change — altered power and a completely new point of view — by abandoning him at the peak of his claim; keeping him in frame with her would hand us the habitual two-shot and let his motion contaminate the stillness that makes her land.

shots.purpose: The wipe that makes it worse — the smear across his eyes is authored here, and it is his own paw that blinds him, so the crash that follows has a visible author.
shots.performanceAssignment: He scrubs with the brisk efficiency of a bee tidying himself for inspection — the paw dragging flat and hard across the band, sweeping the same route twice because a second pass is obviously thoroughness, his eyes screwed shut under the scrubbing and his head turning into each stroke to meet the paw. The drag shears the gold sideways rather than lifting it, banking it up over his eye ridges until it sits across both eyes, and when he opens them he is looking through his own mess: the head makes two quick searching turns, the hover drifting off its line as he does. He does not stop and he does not wipe again. The chest swings forward and the shoulders drag back into the launch position, the hind legs tuck, and he drives forward out of frame on a line he has not looked down — clipping a stem on the way past because he never saw it, the stem snapping back behind him.
shots.camera: Close and travelling with him again, pulled back into the wingman register by his body: as the paw finishes its drag and the chest squares, the camera is already being towed into the launch and loses his line as it goes wide across the corridor. It should be behind and late enough that we do not see what he is about to hit.

shots.purpose: Arrive late on the aftermath — legs kicking above a blossom rim before we ever see what put them there — then let him pop up and announce the sound effect we already heard.
shots.performanceAssignment: Wedged head-first, he treats being stuck as a job in progress: both legs pedal hard above the petal rim, the wings beating fast and shoving against the outside of the petals, and each shove rocks the whole flower on its stem. One leg finds the rim and braces; the brace lets his shoulders drive upward and force the rim wide, and the rim's spring-back dumps the bloom's own packed gold down over the mask he arrived with. He comes up out of it with the head already lifting, drags the chest forward and the shoulders back into the biggest stance in the scene so far, both antennae snapping erect on the accent, and puts the announcement out at full volume with the caked face turned proudly along the corridor — no dusting off, no checking himself, nothing in him treating this as a recovery.
shots.camera: The camera has genuinely missed the crash and admits it: it discovers the kicking legs past a foreground petal, the swinging branch reading behind them as the only evidence of the impact, then the pop-up pushes the frame back as his body comes up. It must not swing over to her at the end — this beat's whole engineering is that the hold she would normally get is being withheld.
shots.openingPose: Bee-height across a blossom cluster, the camera arriving into the aftermath — a branch still swinging in the mid-ground where something was swatted out of the air, and beyond it two legs kicking above a blossom rim, the rest of him buried head-first inside the bloom, gold dust still raining down through the shaft of light between us and him.
shots.cutInMotivation: The cut is the gag: skipping his blind flight and landing in the aftermath makes the audience reconstruct the impact, which the treatment holds is funnier than the impact — staying continuous through the branch and the tumble would show them everything and buy nothing.

shots.performanceAssignment: He is still working the dive when the rumble arrives, and his body takes it before his mind does: one whole side of his flight drops away so he hangs crooked, the altitude sagging low and then over-correcting too high in a single porpoise he never asked for, the caked face swinging as the tilt swings him. shots.camera: The camera anticipates for the first and only time in the scene: it goes to the weather ahead of both bees, then comes back down to Fuzzby late and finds his hover already crooked. shots.performanceAssignment: Her eyes have already gone up above the top of frame and they stay working up there — tracking something crossing above her, one small re-aim as it moves, while every other part of her keeps doing what it was doing: her paws resting on the packed gold of her own sacks, her weight held forward on the leaf, her breathing gone shallower and slower than the shot before. The line comes out of a mouth that moves and a body that does not follow it, level and small, and her eyes never come down off the sky for it. Afterwards her forelegs draw a fraction closer to her body and the antennae angle back a degree — the whole response is a narrowing, and she never turns toward him. The leaf under her takes one small dip and recovers as her weight shifts.

Stillness here is FOR the size of the thing she is naming: the smaller and flatter the frame, the bigger the sky. What lives inside it is the cooling of the haze behind her, the dust in the shaft going dull, and her eyes holding on something above the top of frame while her paws stay on her work.

shots.tempoDesign: The stillest and longest-feeling shot in the scene, and every second of it has something small alive in it. The eyes are already up when the cut lands — no travel to watch, the movement has already happened, which is the economy. The single re-aim of the gaze comes early and is tiny. The line is delivered on one flat unhurried tempo with no accent anywhere in it, and a long beat sits after it before anything else happens. The narrowing — forelegs in, antennae back — takes place slowly across that beat, almost too slow to catch. shots.purpose: The boast IS the launch — and the flower has the last word, closing on him. The only impact with no ride before it, and the only one he cannot cover up, because the cover-up is stuck inside a bloom.
shots.performanceAssignment: The claim and the launch are one movement in him: the chest pumps forward on the answer and the pump itself is what drives him, so he is already travelling as the words go out, antennae proud-erect, hind legs trailing, the line rising and dipping under him without ever levelling. He does not slow, does not look down the line and does not brake — the head and chest drive past the bloom's centre and compress its inner petals, and his own speed rolls the outer petals inward over his shoulders until they fold shut behind him and grip at his waist. What is left outside keeps insisting: his rear half wags side to side against the closed petals as he shoves forward at something he cannot reach, and both wings beat fast and continuous outside the fold, working against a flower that has already won. The wagging gets smaller but does not stop, and the petals do not open.
shots.camera: The camera is his wingman one final time — towed forward on his drive, close and late, and it stays with the flower after he has gone into it rather than following him inside; the petals fold across the lens's view of him and the frame simply keeps watching the closed bloom. Then it lets the far background carry the cost: the cooled sky behind the canopy stays small and sharp in the depth of the same frame, never re-established, and her leaf is never revisited — she does not turn to look and the camera does not go to ask her.
shots.openingPose: Bee-height in the corridor with Fuzzby driving forward into the shot from behind the lens, chest pumped on the boast, and dead ahead of him in the mid-ground an open flower waiting wide — cooling grey-green haze filling the corridor beyond it, gold light thinning across the petals.

output.frameLogic:
THE DIRECTOR, PLAIN WORDS FIRST.

(1) WHAT IS THIS FRAME FOR? In the first half-second a four-year-old should feel the floor drop — we are already moving, already behind someone who is going too fast, and stems are coming at us. Not "here is a bee", but "we are IN it". And over the top of the frame, the parent clocks the leaf ceiling pressing down on him and knows, without being told, that this ends badly. The frame is a promise of trouble made by crowding, not by anything anyone does.

(2) WHAT MUST THIS FRAME AFFORD? Twelve seconds of chained physics land on this stage, so the stage has to have the room and the objects already in it:
 · A LANE UP AND AWAY. He is mid-zig-zag, climbing. The performance's first move is up-and-forward into the next porpoise beat, so the upper-middle depth of the corridor must be genuinely open air — I do not decorate that lane. But the ceiling of leaves closes it a short way above him, so the climb has somewhere to go and something to threaten him.
 · THE OBJECTS THE CHAIN NEEDS, PRESENT AND REACHABLE, NOT INVENTED LATER: the target blossom must already be visible ahead up-corridor (he attacks it at the dip); and the BROAD LEAF that takes him — the one whose stalk bows and snaps — must already be hanging in the mid-corridor, on its own stalk, on the side his weighted exit will drag him toward. If those two are not in the plate now, the render invents them mid-shot and the "one cause" reads as bad luck.
 · A NEAR-FIELD STEM SWINGING BACK ACROSS THE LENS. This is the whole "camera is his wingman, half a beat late" grammar stated in one physical object, and it is also the swipe-close danger the felt intent asks for. It must be caught mid-swing-back, still travelling, so motion can continue out of it.
 · DEPTH TO THE HORIZON OF THE CORRIDOR. Zenny lives at the far end. She is not in this beat and must not be looked at — but the corridor has to actually run that far back or the payoff has nowhere to put her.
 · THE ANCHOR FOR THE CHARACTER NOT DRIVING THE ACTION. Zenny is not a spot in the background; she is welded to her own blossom, settled on its rim, sacks loaded, head down into the cup. Whatever that flower does, she goes with it.
 · Fuzzby placed off-centre and off-edge — low-left-of-centre, pitched away from us — so there is air above, air ahead and air behind him. He must NOT be level or controlled: this is mid-climb, nose up, body rolled with the zig.

craft_notes: The whole take runs off one cause — his chest driving ahead of his wings — and every later event is a consequence of it: his wake rocks the clover, the clover takes Zenny down, his own speed delivers him into the bloom, the stem's whip throws him out, the second bloom rolls him into the somersaults. The chain connects link to link without needing 'then' to bolt two shots together.

There is essentially one stillness instruction in the whole brief — the crisp arrested beat on the landing — and it is the one the director explicitly asked for. Zenny, who is not travelling, is given a continuous job (head in the florets, sacks filling, riding the sway of the clover) rather than being told to stay put, so she will read alive in the background instead of frozen.

The biggest movement sits inside the dialogue rather than after it: the flight-out runs under the opening spoken section and the superhero pose is where the final spoken section lands, so nothing parks to talk.

output.openingFrameRead:
(1) WHAT KIND OF PLACE: a wide-open wildflower meadow, no walls, no ceiling, no corridor and no canopy — the paperwork in the legacy block says "corridor of tall rainforest flowers" and the picture plainly is not that, so I write the picture. Open sky and a low sun burning in from upper right, flaring across the frame in soft bloom and floating motes; you can see far — banks of lavender spikes, white daisies, magenta and red clover heads receding into a hazy sunlit bank behind. Underfoot, crowding the bottom two-thirds, is a dense thicket of blooms at bee height: daisy faces, clover globes, yellow buttercup-ish petals, thick green stems and leaves. Overhead is nothing but light and air.
(2) WHERE IS EACH CHARACTER: both hovering front-on, dead centre band of frame, at flower-top height, and crucially at the SAME distance from the lens — Fuzzby left of centre, clearly the larger and rounder, spectacles catching the backlight, wings blurred; Zenny to his right, noticeably smaller, spectacles, rosy cheeks, wings blurred, positioned directly above a clover head. Sharing depth is what makes the size gap readable, and it is fragile.
(3) WHAT THIS FRAME AFFORDS: enormous lateral and deep room — he can drive out across the meadow and shrink to a dot without leaving frame, because the field runs to the far hazy bank. Blooms are within a body-length of both bees in every direction: a big daisy face and a clover globe near frame-right of him, more clustered mid-frame, all close enough to be hit, engulfed, clipped and landed on at exactly this height. Zenny's clover is directly under her, one drop away.
(4) WHERE IT GOES: it ends on a completely different image the opening frame could not show — Zenny alone and much larger in frame, settled at her clover with full pollen sacks, head lifting to look straight down the lens with a shrug and the smallest smile, while Fuzzby is left behind her, soft, dusty gold and frozen in a superhero pose on a flower head.
output.providerPrompt:
ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Use @Audio1 as the sole source of dialogue, wording, voice, performance and timing. Fuzzby is the only speaker; Zenny never speaks and her mouth stays closed throughout. No additional speech, no added words, no other voice — Fuzzby's flight buzz, breath and the meadow's ambient bed run continuously underneath.

Reference roles: @图1 only for the exact opening composition and positions; @图3 only for Fuzzby's identity, proportions, features and accessories — match the reference 100%, every feature and accessory exactly as shown; @图2 only for Zenny's identity, proportions, features and accessories — match the reference 100%, every feature and accessory exactly as shown; @图4 only for the world.

Shot 1: 50mm, front-on, one camera position for almost the whole take — the frame breathes and reframes a few inches to keep the wreck and Zenny in it, nothing more — then ONE motivated dolly in at the very end. Begin exactly on @图1. Wide-open wildflower meadow, low sun flaring in from upper right, open sky above the flower tops, the thicket of lavender spikes, daisy faces and clover globes crowded across the lower frame; motes drift through the flare. Both bees share the same distance from the lens so Fuzzby reads plainly as the bigger bee and Zenny as the smaller one — keep them at that shared depth until the dolly.

Motion begins on the first frame. During the opening spoken section of @Audio1, Fuzzby's chest drives out ahead of his own wings and hauls him away from her across the meadow at full pace, his wake bending the daisy faces he passes; the bent daisies mark his line as it swings wide and erratic, up over the flower tops and down among them again, no two beats the same length, until he has shrunk to a fast dot skimming the far blooms — still inside frame, never above the flower tops into empty sky. As he leaves, the draught off him rocks the clover under Zenny, and the rocking clover takes her down onto it: she folds her wings, plants on the globe, dips her head into the florets and works, pollen sacks filling, and whenever that clover head sways she travels physically with it. She does not look up. Not once.

The far dot swells fast — he comes back harder than he left, growing across the frame with the near blooms bowing away from him — and drives FACE-FIRST into a big flower head at full speed, his own speed delivering him into it. FWUMP. The petals, flower head and stem behave as one connected flexible structure: the bloom folds completely around him and swallows him whole, hiding him for a clear beat while the head rocks heavily on its loaded stem, the stem bowing then whipping back — and that whip releases him out the far side, plastered and trailing thick gold behind him in a rope. Half-blind, limbs loose and wings helpless, he is a passenger now, not a performer. His shoulder clips a second bloom off-centre; the bloom rolls him, and the roll becomes THREE fast tight somersaults — one, two, three, readable as three, limbs tucked, spectacles and wings and round silhouette legible through every rotation, gold shearing off him into the air — all of it down among the blooms at flower height with Zenny at work in frame beside him.

He comes out of the third rotation feet-first and STICKS it on a sturdy flower head like a gymnast finishing a routine: feet planting hard, the flower head dipping once under his weight and holding him, one leg tucked back for balance, everything about him arrested for one crisp beat while the gold he shed keeps falling past. THUP.

Then he rises up out of it. Quick embarrassed little pats — chest, arms, chest again — knock puffs of pollen off him; the puffs hang in the flare. His head snaps left, snaps right, checking whether anyone saw, and finding himself completely intact he SNAPS into a full superhero pose: chest out one notch and then another, fists planted, shoulders squared, chin up, one antenna proud-erect and one folded over and refusing to rise, wings still beating fast beneath all that dignity. The final spoken section of @Audio1 lands on that pose, gold still drifting off his glasses, small mid-air corrections twitching under his feet as the flower head takes his swagger.

And the camera leaves him. It dollies in past him and onto Zenny alone at her clover, letting him slide soft and dusty behind her, still on parade in his own falling gold — she grows in frame, sacks full, and lifts her head for the first time in the whole take, looks STRAIGHT DOWN THE LENS, gives one small shrug of her shoulders, and lets the smallest smile arrive at the corner of her mouth. Low sun rims her fur from behind; soft bounce off the white daisy below warms her face; catchlights sit bright in her eyes.

No glow, no sparkle trail, no magic light on either bee. No cut anywhere in the take. Hold on Zenny looking down the lens for two seconds after the audio finishes — her wings and the meadow still moving, pollen still falling behind her. No further speech.
output.doesItLand: Yes — the crash is written as a full-body swallow rather than a brush, the three somersaults and the stuck landing arrive as one unbroken chain of his own momentum, and because Zenny never lifts her head until the dolly reaches her, her look down the lens is the only new information in the frame and takes the laugh clean off his pose.

envelope.prompt:
Wide shot, 24mm, bee-height inside a corridor of tall rainforest flowers, camera low and slightly behind and beneath Fuzzby and already travelling forward with him, horizon rolled with his bank — a chase frame, half a beat late on its subject. One frozen instant.

Fuzzby is the character from @图3 — match the reference; at this size that is silhouette, proportion and colour, not features. He sits low-left of centre, mid-zig-zag and climbing: body pitched nose-up and away from camera in three-quarter rear, rolled into the turn, hind legs braced beneath him with a loose rope of gold dust streaming off them and back toward the lens, wings a fast blur on both sides. Nothing about him is level or settled — he is on the way up, off-centre, clear of every frame edge, with open corridor air above and ahead of him.

Zenny is the character from @图2 — match the reference; at this size that is silhouette, proportion and colour, not features. She is tiny and soft far back down the corridor at the limit of focus, settled on the rim of her own blossom with loaded pollen sacks, head down into the cup, unremarked and unlit by anything special — physically perched on that flower, travelling with it.

Scale: both bees are small against botanical giants — stems thicker than their bodies, blossoms wider than their wingspan, the corridor towering past the top of frame.

Foreground: a thick flower stem swings back across the near lens frame-right, caught mid-swing where he has just clipped it, its leaf still cocked from the strike — huge, soft-focused, close enough to swipe. A second stem rakes the left edge. Midground: the corridor of stems opens into clear flying air up and frame-right, and hanging on its own stalk out to the right of that lane, a broad flat leaf sits alone in his flight path, its stalk long and springy and unloaded. Up-corridor beyond it, the target blossom stands open with its anthers heavy and loose with gold. Background: the corridor recedes in receding layers of stems and blooms to Zenny's distant flower, everything beyond her dissolving into soft green haze. Overhead: a low ceiling of broad leaves crowds the top of frame and presses down close over his back, leaving him almost no headroom the whole way up the corridor.

Light per the scene's locked state — low sun just above the hills, long gold light raking the flower tops — broken here into hard shafts falling through the leaf ceiling and striping the corridor floor to ceiling, bright bars alternating with deep green shade so the passage reads as strobing light; loose motes hang in every shaft; the near stems are rimmed bright along one edge and fall to dark toward the lens. Palette, materials and light exactly as @图4.

Stylised feature-quality 3D CGI, Pixar-caliber, real weight and bold legible staging, characters locked to their references. No text, no extra characters, no crystals on the bees.

The read: we are already inside somebody's ride, going too fast to see him properly, with the roof coming down.

Add no additional SPEECH, no extra words and no narration — but the bees' own wing-buzz runs unbroken throughout, and Zenny's one long audible out-breath near the end is directed, not forbidden.

@图1 only for the exact opening composition and positions; @图3 only for Fuzzby's identity, proportions, features and accessories; @图2 only for Zenny's identity, proportions, features and accessories; @图4 only for the world. Fuzzby is the character from @图3 — match the reference 100%, every feature and accessory exactly as shown. Zenny is the character from @图2 — match the reference 100%, every feature and accessory exactly as shown. Stylised feature-quality 3D CGI for ages 4–8: real weight, appealing squash-and-stretch, bold readable silhouettes. Low sun flares in behind them from the upper right, open sky above the flower tops, the crowded bed of lavender spikes, daisies and clover heads filling the lower frame. No glow, no sparkle trail, no magic light on either bee.

Shot 1: front-on wide two-shot at flower-top height, 35mm, one camera position that only breathes and reframes a few inches to keep the wreck and Zenny both in frame — until its one real move at the very end. Begin exactly on @图1 and let motion continue immediately with no resting beat. Fuzzby's wings load, his chest drives out ahead of them, and on the opening spoken section of @Audio1 he tears away frame right at full pace, mouth working the song, clearing the frame entirely on that one readable line. The camera does not follow him and does not go looking. Zenny's eyes travel out after him, hold on the empty air a moment, then give up on him — her head drops and she lowers onto the clover head beneath her, forelegs working the florets, busy and unhurried, head down, and from here she rides that clover: whenever it bends or nods she travels physically with it.

Then the far flower tops flick and part as something comes back along them — he re-enters from the SAME edge he left, at the same height, faster than he went, and misjudges everything. A lavender stem clips his trailing wing and the clip yaws his whole body off its line; the yaw throws his head out in front of him; that wing corrects far too late, and the late correction drives his face square into the pollen centre of a big daisy at full speed. The petal, flower head and stem are one flexible connected structure and they take the whole force: the head compresses flat beneath him, the stem bows most of the way to the ground, the petals splay backwards, and a fat cloud of gold bursts out sideways and knocks the neighbouring blooms nodding. His body, wings and spectacles stay OUTSIDE the bloom and readable in silhouette through all of it — only his face and the front of his chest ever touch the pollen; the flower never swallows or hides him. The loaded stem whips upright and flings him off it, coated thick in gold and trailing it behind him.

Still travelling and half blind, his shoulder catches a second flower head and that contact turns him over — the turn becomes three fast tight somersaults, readable as three, limbs tucked, wings helpless: he is a passenger, not a performer, and every rotation happens down among the blooms at flower height, never up in open sky, with Zenny working head-down in shot the whole time. The third rotation spits him out feet-first onto a sturdy clover head and he plants hard, one leg tucked back behind him like a gymnast finishing a routine — the head dips deep under his weight and rebounds, and his balance rides that rebound with small corrections, wings beating fast inside the held tension. Nothing about him stops moving.

He stands up out of the finish, beats the gold off his chest with two quick swipes, and one fast embarrassed glance goes round the flowers to check whether anyone saw. Finding himself completely fine, he snaps into a full superhero pose — chest out, fists planted on hips, chin up, shoulders squared, dusty and delighted — and the final spoken section of @Audio1 lands exactly on that pose, his chest pushing out one further notch on it while gold still falls past him. Zenny does not look up.

As his line finishes, the camera leaves him and dollies in on Zenny alone, her clover filling the frame and Fuzzby dropping soft and out of focus behind her, still on parade on his flower head with pollen drifting. Her eyes come up first and find him. Then her body receives it: her chest rises and falls in one long, entirely deadpan sigh. Her face does not change. She holds that flatness a beat longer than is comfortable — and only then, as she turns fractionally back toward the lens, does ONE corner of her mouth go, dry and private, never broad, never warm, never a finished smile. Hold on that corner still moving, on Zenny sharp and Fuzzby soft behind her, for two seconds after the audio finishes — wing-buzz, drifting pollen and nodding blooms carry on. No further speech.
